question: How do sports doctors tell overtraining syndrome apart from ordinary heavy fatigue?
answer: Mostly in hindsight. No blood test or marker settles it, so the diagnosis is made by ruling out other causes, and the clearest difference is how long recovery takes: days to weeks after functional overreaching, weeks to months after the non-functional kind, and months or longer in the full syndrome. The calendar gives the label.
move: When no test separates two states, watch how long each one lasts.
source: Meeusen et al., ECSS and ACSM consensus, 2013
reference: Meeusen et al., Prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of the overtraining syndrome: joint consensus statement of the ECSS and the ACSM, Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise, 2013
